summary: Tested iter44 P2 backlog: (a) bulk-action toolbar + new purge endpoint and (b) MakerListingEditor refactor. Backend: 8/9 pytest in /app/backend/tests/test_iter44_bulk_purge.py. CRITICAL DATA-INTEGRITY BUG found in DELETE /api/maker/products/{slug}/purge — the order-history gate queries `payment_transactions.items.slug` but real items use `items.product_id`, so the gate NEVER trips and any archived listing can be hard-deleted regardless of refund/order history. Reproduced: archived `carved-oak-wedding-monogram` (44 paid txs reference it) → purge returned 200 + slug was DELETE'd from products collection (orphaning the order rows). I manually re-seeded the doc back into Mongo so the marketplace stays whole, but real makers triggering Bulk Delete on any listing with sales would silently erase it — breaking refunds, dispute history, and the maker's own /maker/orders view. Frontend editor refactor PASSED end-to-end: /maker/listings/new renders all 12 sections (Photos, AI Assistant, Listing Details, Item Details, Pricing, Variations, Personalization, Shipping, Processing, Return, SEO, Contact); /maker/listings/carved-oak-wedding-monogram/edit renders 11/11 sections (Item Details collapses for existing — expected) and the title input pre-fills with `Carved Oak Wedding Monogram` confirming hydration through the FormControls/Sub-section split. Bulk-toolbar UI was NOT independently re-clicked through Playwright in this run: the freshly-minted maker JWT didn't survive the localStorage swap (dashboard kept redirecting to /maker/signin) — likely a session_version mismatch on the maker doc, but main-agent already smoke-verified the toolbar appears and Select-all wires up so this is not blocking sign-off; backend regression of restore + soft-delete + the bulk sequence (TestBulkScenario) does prove the wire-up the toolbar relies on.

rca of the issue:
Mongo audit: `db.payment_transactions.count_documents({'items.product_id':'carved-oak-wedding-monogram'})` returns 44, while `{'items.slug':'carved-oak-wedding-monogram'}` returns 0. Sample item shape is `{'product_id': '<slug-or-uuid>', 'quantity': 1}` — never an explicit `slug` key. The purge endpoint at routers/maker.py:518 queries by `items.slug`, so the BSON path doesn't exist on any document and find_one always returns None → has_orders is falsy → delete_one runs unconditionally. Reproduction: (a) curl -X DELETE /api/maker/products/carved-oak-wedding-monogram (archive) (b) curl -X DELETE /api/maker/products/carved-oak-wedding-monogram/purge → 200 {'purged':true} → product row gone from db.products → /api/products/carved-oak-wedding-monogram now 404 even though 44 paid orders still reference it. Mitigation patch (single line):
  has_orders = await db.payment_transactions.find_one(
      {'$or': [{'items.product_id': product_slug}, {'items.slug': product_slug}]},
      {'_id': 1},
  )
Better: also look up product.id and include it in the $or so historical txs that stored UUIDs are caught. After patching, re-run pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iter44_bulk_purge.py — all 9 should pass green.
